fields.title: «Polka»: twenty minutes due to ratings
fields.summary: 22 minutes of complete outage due to the reviews service. This is the third cascade in half a year.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. Yesterday at 19:40 the product was completely down for 22 minutes. Around 980 orders lost. Root cause: review service database started rebuilding its index, responses slowed down to 25 seconds. After 9 minutes the catalog stopped opening, after 14 minutes the home screen stopped. You are running the post-mortem and proposing what to do.
fields.brief/objective: Eliminate not this specific cascade, but the possibility of a cascade—before connecting new chains.
fields.brief/constraints: Three weeks of systematic work compete with the product roadmap.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do and how you guarantee the system work won't be postponed again.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: A third similar failure is not a coincidence
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A cascade consists of two things: a synchronous call without a timeout and no alert for an 'unimportant' service. While they are fixed case by case, the next cascade comes from somewhere else. The sign that it is time to fix the class, not the case, is simple: something similar has happened before, and each time it was explained differently.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Provides store rating and review count on the card. Research shows it affects conversion by about 3%.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Catalog requests ratings when rendering cards, synchronously, no timeout. Home screen calls catalog.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "Timeout - a day of work. Pool cutoff - two days. Ratings cache with TTL 30 minutes - three days, will remove 95% of calls. Emergency toggle for the rating block - a day."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Review slowdown was visible on charts starting at 19:31. No alert—it wasn't configured for this service, considered unimportant.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Fix this call: timeout plus circuit breaker for ratings
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Fix this call: timeout plus circuit breaker for ratings. Two days.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: this scenario is closed. The fourth cascade will come from somewhere else—this is the third incident, and each time they only fixed the specific spot.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Rating cache with 30 min TTL. Three days.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: 95% of calls never reach the service, the impact of its failure drops sharply. Does not solve the class problem: any uncached call remains dangerous. Ratings get half an hour old—unnoticeable.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Systematically: timeouts and bulkheads on all inter-service calls plus circuit breakers plus alerts
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Systematically: timeouts and bulkheads on all inter-service calls plus circuit breakers plus alerts. Three weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: closes the class of problems, not just the case. Finishes before connecting chains. Three weeks of team effort competing with the product roadmap.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Timeout and breaker now, system work next quarter
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Timeout and breaker now, system work next quarter. Two days plus a plan.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: immediate patch, systemic work later. Risk that «later» never happens, because it already happened twice.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not understand cascade failure mechanics
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not see caching as a way to reduce failure impact
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Did not design degradation with a circuit breaker
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Cascade is not analyzed as a failure class, treated as isolated cases
